class.name: DirectionalBulletsData2D
class.description: Ensure that the [member MultiMeshBulletsData2D.transforms] and [member all_bullet_speed_data] are set, otherwise spawning fails with an error and no bullets are created (an empty speed array fails; give one entry per bullet). [b]How per-bullet and shared work together:[/b] every [code]all_bullet_*[/code] array is indexed by bullet: entry [code]i[/code] belongs to bullet [code]i[/code] and nobody else. Each bullet resolves on its own: a valid per-bullet entry wins for that bullet; otherwise the matching [code]shared_*[/code] value fills in when it is set; otherwise the feature default applies (speed 0, no spin, no curves, straight flight, no gravity, null custom data). A short array only covers its own indices — the remaining bullets fall back. A long array ignores the extras. Size mismatches warn once per spawn but never block it. [b]Invalid entries[/b] never poison their siblings: null entries, wrong-typed resources, NaN/Inf numbers, disabled wobble seeds, and unresolvable pattern paths each fall back for that bullet only. [b]Tiling (opt-in):[/b] every array below has a [code]tile_*[/code] checkbox next to it in the inspector (off by default). When checked, a short array wraps around the volley for that array only: bullet [code]i[/code] reads entry [code]i % size[/code], so 2 entries fan across 10 bullets as A,B,A,B... Invalid entries still fall back per bullet. [b]Migration:[/b] older setups that relied on a single entry covering every bullet no longer get that for free. Either provide one entry per bullet, set the [code]shared_*[/code] value (it covers every bullet the array leaves out), or check the [code]tile_*[/code] box for that array. Check [MultiMeshBulletsData2D]'s documentation for the rest of the properties.

members.member: If enabled, the bullets will adjust their direction when rotating, instead of only spinning in place.

Curves for each bullet, applied at spawn time (and on pool reuse). Entry [code]i[/code] drives bullet [code]i[/code] only. Bullets without an entry (short array) or with a null entry use [member shared_bullet_curves_data] per channel, or plain ballistics when that is unset too. Invalid means: null entry. Example: 4 bullets, entries [A, null] → bullets 0 and 1 use A and the shared fallback, bullets 2 and 3 use the shared fallback only.

When on, a short [member all_bullet_curves_data] wraps around the volley (bullet [code]i[/code] reads entry [code]i % size[/code]) instead of leaving the tail bullets on the fallback. Off by default. Example: 2 entries across 10 bullets fan as A,B,A,B...

Face flag for each bullet's own pattern. Entry [code]i[/code] belongs to bullet [code]i[/code]; bullets without an entry use [member shared_movement_pattern_face_movement_direction]. Has its own [member tile_all_bullet_movement_pattern_face_movement_directions] checkbox.
When on, a short face-flag array wraps around the volley instead of leaving the tail bullets on the shared flag. Off by default.

Pattern path for each bullet, applied at spawn time (and on pool reuse). Each entry must point at a [Path2D]; its [Curve2D] is extracted when the volley spawns. Entry [code]i[/code] drives bullet [code]i[/code] only. A bullet with its own valid pattern always uses it; [member shared_movement_pattern_path] only covers bullets without one. Empty or bad entries fall back per bullet. Example: give bullet 0 a loop curve and leave the rest empty → only bullet 0 loops, the rest fly the shared pattern (or straight when that is empty too).
When on, short pattern-path arrays wrap around the volley instead of leaving the tail bullets on the shared pattern. Off by default.

Repeat flag for each bullet's own pattern. Entry [code]i[/code] belongs to bullet [code]i[/code]; bullets without an entry use [member shared_movement_pattern_repeat]. Has its own [member tile_all_bullet_movement_pattern_repeats] checkbox.
When on, a short repeat-flag array wraps around the volley instead of leaving the tail bullets on the shared flag. Off by default.

[b]MANDATORY[/b] Speed for each bullet — entry [code]i[/code] drives bullet [code]i[/code] only, so give one entry per bullet (same size as [member MultiMeshBulletsData2D.transforms]). Bullets without a valid entry fall back to [member shared_bullet_speed_data], or fly at speed 0 when that is unset. Invalid means: null entry, or NaN/Inf speed, max_speed or acceleration (that bullet reads 0/0/0, its siblings are untouched). Negative speed is legal and flies backwards along the heading. Example: 3 bullets, speeds [200, null, 200] with shared 150 → bullets fly at 200, 150, 200. Note: [BulletSpeedData2D] has a helper static method that you can use to generate random speed data - [method BulletSpeedData2D.generate_random_data()].

When on, a short [member all_bullet_speed_data] wraps around the volley (bullet [code]i[/code] reads entry [code]i % size[/code]) instead of falling back. Off by default. Example: 2 entries across 10 bullets fan as A,B,A,B... Use it for alternating spreads without writing 10 entries.

Wobble seed for each bullet, applied at spawn time (and on pool reuse). Entry [code]i[/code] affects bullet [code]i[/code] only; a live seed always beats [member shared_bullet_wobble_data] for its bullet. Null entries and entries with [code]enabled = false[/code] fall back to shared for that bullet. Example: shared gentle weave plus one strong seed on bullet 2 → bullet 2 snakes hard, the rest weave gently.
When on, a short [member all_bullet_wobble_data] wraps around the volley instead of leaving the tail bullets on the shared fallback. Off by default.
Per-bullet queue: pop the front target when the owning bullet reaches it. Pooled reuse re-seeds this from the spawn data, so direct [BulletFactory2D] spawns keep it without a spawner.

Fallback gravity in px/s^2 for bullets without their own [member all_bullet_gravity] entry (2D sideview arcs, tower-defense shells). (0, 0) disables — top-down default. Must stay finite. Example: shared (0, 1000) plus per-bullet [(0,0), (800,0)] on 3 bullets → bullet 0 hovers, bullet 1 drifts right, bullet 2 falls.
Gravity for each bullet. Entry [code]i[/code] pulls bullet [code]i[/code] only. Empty (default) means every bullet uses [member gravity]. A non-finite entry reads as (0, 0) for that bullet only.
When on, a short [member all_bullet_gravity] wraps around the volley instead of leaving the tail bullets on [member gravity]. Off by default.
Seconds of straight flight before gravity starts integrating (shells that glide first, then drop). 0 falls immediately.
Seconds of falling before gravity stops integrating (shells that drop, then glide on with frozen fall speed). 0 = infinite.
Seconds of straight flight before homing steering starts (classic aimed-then-homing). 0 steers immediately.

Distance in pixels at which a bullet counts as having reached its target (drives the reached signal and auto-pop). Tested against the final steered position, so locked orbiting bullets test their orbit motion.
Seconds of steering before bullets fly straight (lets fast players escape). 0 = infinite.
Steering pauses while the bullet is farther than this from its target. 0 = unlimited.
Shared homing turn agility (0 snaps instantly). Pooled reuse re-seeds this from the spawn data. Setting any per-bullet smoothing on the live volley switches it to per-bullet mode.
Whether homing steers the bullet facing. Leave off when a movement pattern, rotation data, or orbiting texture mode already owns the facing, otherwise homing steers nothing visible.
Seconds between homing target position refreshes (0 refreshes every tick). Larger values make rings lag and step on moving targets; keep 0 for bodyguard rings.
Linear drag trimming speed each tick (speed -= speed * drag * delta). 0 disables. Must be finite and >= 0.

Fallback curves, resolved per channel at spawn time (and on pool reuse). A bullet that carries its own x-curve uses it even when this also defines x; this only covers the channels the bullet lacks. Null (default) means no fallback — uncovered channels fly plain ballistics. Example: shared defines x-drift plus a speed ramp, bullet 2 carries only a y-curve → bullet 2 flies with its own y plus the shared x and speed.

Fallback spin for bullets whose own rotation entry is missing or invalid (null, or NaN/Inf values), applied at spawn time (and on pool reuse). A valid per-bullet entry always wins for its bullet. Null (default) means no fallback — uncovered bullets don't rotate. Example: rotation entries [1.0, null] with shared 5.0 → bullet 0 spins at 1.0, bullet 1 at 5.0.

Fallback speed for bullets whose own speed entry is missing or invalid (null, or NaN/Inf values), applied at spawn time (and on pool reuse). A valid per-bullet entry always wins for its bullet. Null (default) means no fallback — uncovered bullets fly at speed 0. Example: speeds [200, null, 200] with shared 150 → bullets fly at 200, 150, 200. Note: shared movement-speed curves still outrank it per tick.

Fallback wobble for bullets whose own entry is missing, null, or disabled, applied at spawn time (and on pool reuse). A bullet with an active per-bullet seed always uses it. Null (default) means no fallback — uncovered bullets fly straight. Phase fans out per bullet so one resource makes snakes and petals; pick Sine vs Cosine on the resource's waveform.
Shared queue: one deferred pop when any bullet reaches the front target. Locked orbit rings follow the lock policy on the new front instead of holding a stale center.

Fallback face flag for bullets without their own entry in [member all_bullet_movement_pattern_face_movement_directions]. Whether those bullets rotate to face their direction of travel along the pattern.

Fallback pattern for bullets without their own entry in [member all_bullet_movement_pattern_paths]: the [Path2D] in the scene tree whose curve those bullets follow at spawn time (and on pool reuse). Resolved relative to the [BulletFactory2D] with a scene-root fallback; absolute paths always work. Empty (default) means no fallback. Example: shared S-curve plus bullet 0 carrying its own loop → bullet 0 loops, the rest fly the S.
Fallback repeat flag for bullets without their own entry in [member all_bullet_movement_pattern_repeats]. Whether those bullets loop the pattern instead of stopping at the end of the curve.
